Hi Avery,

Thanks for taking the SIG. We're finishing our vendor review for a potential platform rollout and have a couple of focused follow-ups on data persistence and training:

1) Prompt/log archival: Can you confirm Redwood's default retention for prompt logs and whether any automated backups or long-term archives might retain customer content beyond that TTL? Specifically, does your hosted offering create snapshots/backups that could persist prompts beyond the configured retention?

2) KV/prefix caches: Are any KV caches written to durable storage for debugging or debugging-only snapshots? If so, what are the TTLs and controls?

3) Model training: Please confirm whether Redwood uses customer prompts, user messages, or embeddings for model training or fine-tuning by default. If not, what process/contractual opt-in or exceptions exist?

4) Evidence: If possible, please include an architecture diagram and any artifacts (SIG spreadsheet, short attestation) we can attach to our procurement file.

Hi Jessica — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Lauren, Priyom, and Steph for engineering and legal confirmation; below are concise answers and an initial attachments bundle. Attaching: redwood_sig_answers_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet mapping SIG rows to our controls).

Quick answers (summary):
- Prompt/log retention: Hosted default retention for request and response logs (text payloads) is 30 days. Customers can configure shorter retention or opt for immediate deletion on a per-account basis for hosted accounts.
- Backups/archives: We do NOT create separate long-term archives of user prompts in hosted by default. Service backups (storage-level snapshots) exclude request bodies and only persist encrypted system metadata necessary for recovery. Backups are encrypted at rest and have automated rotation; retention for backup metadata is up to 90 days.
- KV/prefix caches: Runtime KV caches (used for latency-sensitive prefix caching) are in-memory by default and are ephemeral; we do not persist KV caches to durable storage except when a customer explicitly enables persistence for Private/Dedicated deployments. In Private deployments persistence is configurable and must be approved in the runbook.
- Model training: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts, responses, or embeddings for training or model fine-tuning unless there is explicit contractual opt-in and an internal approval workflow (legal + research + product). Aggregated telemetry (non-identifiable usage stats) can be used to improve platform reliability, but not model weights.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached redwood_sig_answers_v1.xlsx — it's a mapping to SIG questions and references to our SOC 2 and CAIQ artifacts.
2) If you need an architecture diagram, I've asked Priyom to attach our brief KV/cache archival diagram (will follow in this thread).

If anything above needs to be more formal (signed attestation), we can route through contracts. Happy to set up a 30-min call.

Hi Jessica — answering the clarifications below and attaching an updated bundle (redwood_sig_answers_v2.xlsx + kv-ephemeral-archival-design.pdf):

1) Storage-level snapshots: Our production backup policy intentionally excludes request bodies. In our hosted architecture request/response payloads are written to an object store partitioned and lifecycle-managed for short retention. Crash-consistent snapshots are taken at the storage layer, but those snapshots only reference object-store manifests and encrypted metadata; object contents that include request bodies are subject to the configured lifecycle and are not captured separately into a long-term backup blob. Engineering has validated this in our backup runbooks and we can provide the runbook excerpt under NDA or via a secure share.

2) Dedicated/Private defaults: For Dedicated we recommend a 30-day rolling retention for request logs (same as hosted default) unless customer requests a different policy in contract. For Private (customer-managed) the baseline we ship is ephemeral-in-memory caches and disk-backed logs with TTL defaults of 30 days; persistence must be turned on explicitly during installation and we document the recommended settings in the deployment guide. If MedCore requires a shorter baseline, we can deliver a hardened runbook and console policy that enforces immediate deletion.

3) Contractual opt-in language for training: Example clause we use in our SOW/addendum: “Vendor will not use Customer Content to train or tune machine learning models without the Customer’s prior written consent. Aggregated, de‑identified usage metrics may be used to improve platform reliability but will not be used to update model weights.” We can provide a redlined example for procurement.

4) Attestation & artifacts: Attached redwood_sig_answers_v2.xlsx includes a one-paragraph attestation and references (SOC 2 report ID and CAIQ export). The kv-ephemeral-archival-design.pdf is a short (2-pg) diagram showing where KV caches live (in-memory, optional persistence toggle for Private), and which components write to object storage.

If helpful, we can redact and send the SOC 2 bridge letter and provide a secure link for the full report. I'm available for a 30-minute technical review next week; please propose a couple slots.
